parsed.summary: This paper introduces TIPS, a topological framework that treats the contextual hidden states of prompt tokens in large language models as a point cloud to analyze and steer responses to ill-posed questions. By extracting seven descriptors from zero- and one-dimensional persistent homology, the method achieves improved performance in both binary and fine-grained ill-posedness classification. Furthermore, topology-conditioned activation steering significantly increases the rate of appropriate clarification or abstention responses.

chk_problem.value: Large language models struggle with ill-posed questions (such as those involving ambiguity, under-specification, or conflicting statements) because existing work treats LLM reasoning as a black box.
chk_problem.paper_quote: Ill-posed questions, including those involving ambiguity, under-specification, or conflicting statements, may admit no valid answer or multiple plausible answers, posing a significant challenge for large language models (LLMs) despite their otherwise strong performance.

chk_method.value: TIPS, which treats contextual hidden states of prompt tokens as a point cloud and uses persistent homology to extract topological descriptors of ill-posedness and steer model reasoning.
chk_method.paper_quote: To this end, we study the internal state from a topological perspective by treating the contextual hidden states of its prompt tokens at a single transformer layer as a point cloud, capturing the input problem’s relational structure as encoded by the model.

chk_data.value: AmbigQA for binary ill-posedness detection and CLAMBER for fine-grained 9-way ill-posedness classification, evaluated across eight open-weight models.
chk_data.paper_quote: Evaluation on AmbigQA for binary ill-posedness detection, and on CLAMBER for fine-grained 9-way ill-posedness classification demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed topological representation.

chk_setup.value: Evaluating eight models from four families using five split seeds with 70/10/20 train/validation/test splits.
chk_setup.paper_quote: We evaluate eight models from four families using five split seeds (0–4), with 70/10/20 train/validation/test splits.

chk_primary_result.value: TIPS improved average macro-F1 from 75.51% to 78.60% on AmbigQA, and from 36.64% to 39.44% on CLAMBER 9-way classification.
chk_primary_result.paper_quote: Across eight open-weight models from the Llama, Qwen, Gemma, and Ministral families, our seven H0 and H1 descriptors from a single selected layer improve average macro-F1 score over the strongest baselines from 75.51% to 78.60% on AmbigQA, and from 36.64% to 39.44% on CLAMBER 9-way classification.

chk_secondary_result.value: Topology-conditioned steering improved the steered abstention response rate from 27.43% to 51.15% on average across four dataset-model settings.
chk_secondary_result.paper_quote: Averaged across the four dataset–model settings, topology-conditioned steering improves steered abstention response rate from 27.43% to 51.15%.

chk_baseline.value: The method is compared against AEN, a probing baseline that selects ambiguity-predictive neurons and trains a classifier on their activations.
chk_baseline.paper_quote: We compare against AEN (Zhang et al., 2025), a probing baseline that selects ambiguity-predictive neurons and trains a classifier on their activations.

chk_conclusion.value: Compact token-cloud topology provides an effective, unified representation and steering signal for identifying and handling ill-posed problems in large language models.
chk_conclusion.paper_quote: Together, these results demonstrate that compact token-cloud topology provides an effective, unified representation and steering signal for ill-posed problems.

chk_limitation.value: Incorrect detection or steering may cause unnecessary abstention or degraded responses.
chk_limitation.paper_quote: Incorrect detection or steering may cause unnecessary abstention or degraded responses.
